resource_caps_applied.address_space_ulimit_note: PROTOCOL DEVIATION, DISCLOSED: `ulimit -v 2097152` (the mechanism RUN-SSIQ-a85692-a..-j used to apply specification.maximum_memory_gb=2 on their Linux execution host) is NOT SUPPORTED on this execution host's shell (macOS/Darwin): `ulimit -v 2097152` fails with `setrlimit failed: invalid argument`, a known Darwin limitation (RLIMIT_AS is not settable the same way as on Linux). The wall-clock cap was still applied via `timeout 1000`. No address-space cap was applied at the OS level for this run. This is disclosed as an infrastructure/environment difference, not a silent omission: the run's ACTUAL peak memory use was trivial (STEP (0) graph build on N=203 vertices, immediately followed by a G-0c defer -- no delta_E search, no calibration -- total wall-clock 0.19s), so the absence of an enforced cap did not admit any actual over-budget resource use this run, but the cap-application MECHANISM itself differs from every prior run in this lineage and must not be silently presented as identical.
